question: After four years of checking, how sure were the referees of Thomas Hales's proof of the Kepler conjecture?
options: Certain, as with any accepted proof
answer: 99% certain. Hales's 1998 proof of the densest way to stack spheres ran to hundreds of pages plus long computer calculations, and the twelve referees could not check every step. A chain of thousands of links is only as sure as all of them together. A machine-checked version was finished only in 2014.
move: When a proof outgrows any single reader, certainty becomes a matter of trust.
trap: Treating a proof too long to check as certain by definition.
source: Hales et al., Forum of Mathematics, Pi, 2017
reference: Hales et al., A formal proof of the Kepler conjecture, Forum of Mathematics, Pi 5, e2, 2017
